finalOutput:
I've created the complete single-file CHIP-8 emulator `chip8_ollama-glm-4.7-flash-latest_01.html` with all requested features:

**Core Emulator Features:**
- 4 KB memory with font set loaded at 0x050 and programs at 0x200
- 16 general-purpose registers V0-VF, 16-bit index register I, program counter PC, 16-level call stack
- Delay and sound timers that count down at 60 Hz
- All 35 CHIP-8 opcodes implemented (arithmetic/logic with carry/borrow, shifts, jumps/calls, random, BCD, register save/load, key tests)
- 64×32 display on canvas with sprite XOR drawing and VF collision flag

**UI & Controls:**
- Visual 4×4 keypad with on-screen keys and keyboard mapping (1–F)
- Run, Pause, Single Step, and Reset buttons
- Adjustable instructions-per-frame speed slider (1–100 I/帧)
- File ROM loader accepting .rom/.ch8 files
- Demo ROM button that loads a pre-assembled sprite demo

**Debugger Panel:**
- All registers V0-VF, I, PC, stack contents
- Delay and sound timer values
- Decoded current instruction mnemonic and hex

The emulator is fully self-contained with no external libraries or dependencies.

conversation.contentPreview:
Create a complete single self-contained file `chip8_ollama-glm-4.7-flash-latest_01.html` (HTML + CSS + JavaScript inline;
no external libraries, CDNs, assets or backend). Build a working CHIP-8 emulator.

Implement the interpreter properly: 4 KB of memory with the font set loaded at 0x050 and programs at 0x200,
sixteen 8-bit registers V0 to VF, the 16-bit index register, the program counter, a call stack, and the
delay and sound timers counting down at 60 Hz. Decode and execute the complete instruction set of 35
instructions, including the arithmetic and logic group with the carry and borrow flags in VF, the shift
instructions, jumps and calls, the random instruction, BCD conversion, register save and load, and the key
tests.

The display is 64 by 32 pixels drawn on a canvas scaled to a readable size, with sprites drawn by XOR and
the collision flag set in VF. The 16-key keypad is mapped to a 4 by 4 block of keyboard keys shown in the
interface; key press and release must both reach the emulator.

Include a small demo ROM as a byte array inside the file: a real program, assembled by you, that draws a
sprite and moves or reacts to a key, so that the emulator can be tried without any download. Also allow
loading a ROM from a local file.

Add run, pause, single step and reset controls, an adjustable instructions-per-frame speed, and a debugger
panel showing the registers, the index register, the program counter, the stack and the decoded current
instruction. Every visible control must work. Deliver the one file `chip8_ollama-glm-4.7-flash-latest_01.html`.

{"thought":"Goal: build a complete, single-file CHIP-8 emulator in HTML+JS, no external dependencies.

Core requirements:
- 4 KB RAM, font set at 0x050, programs start at 0x200
- 16 general-purpose registers V0-VF, I (16-bit), PC, stack, delay/sound timers (60 Hz)
- Implement all 35 CHIP-8 opcodes (arithmetic/logic with carry/borrow, shifts, jumps/calls, random, BCD, register save/load, key tests)
- 64x32 display on canvas, sprite XOR, VF collision flag

- Demo ROM embedded as byte array (sprite + key reaction)
- File ROM loader
- Controls: run, pause, single step, reset, speed slider
- Debugger: registers, I, PC, stack, decoded instruction

Implementation plan:
1) Data structures: memory array (4096 bytes), registers object, PC, I, stack[], timers
2) Font set: 5x8 binary patterns for 0-F
3) Opcodes: switch on top 12 bits, decode nibbles, execute with flags
4) Timers: decrement every 16.67ms (60 Hz), separate delay/sound
5) Display: canvas 64x32, scale to fit, clear and draw frame
6) Sprite: load byte array, 8 bits per row, XOR to display, set VF if collision
7) Keypad: 16-key array, event listeners, key state tracking
8) CPU loop: fetch -> decode -> execute, variable instruction rate
9) Demo ROM: simple program (sprite drawing, key checking)
10) UI: layout with canvas, keypad, controls, debugger panel
11) File loader: FileReader API, parse hex bytes, load into memory
12) Step-by-step: single-step mode, pause state

I will create the single HTML file with all CSS and JS inline."}

Goal: build a complete, single-file CHIP-8 emulator in HTML+JS, no external dependencies.

Core requirements:
- 4 KB RAM, font set at 0x050, programs start at 0x200
- 16 general-purpose registers V0-VF, I (16-bit), PC, stack, delay/sound timers (60 Hz)
- Implement all 35 CHIP-8 opcodes (arithmetic/logic with carry/borrow, shifts, jumps/calls, random, BCD, register save/load, key tests)
- 64x32 display on canvas, sprite XOR, VF collision flag
- 4x4 keypad with visual keys, keydown/keyup events
- Demo ROM embedded as byte array (sprite + key reaction)
- File ROM loader
- Controls: run, pause, single step, reset, speed slider
- Debugger: registers, I, PC, stack, decoded instruction

Implementation plan:
1) Data structures: memory array (4096 bytes), registers object, PC, I, stack[], timers
2) Font set: 5x8 binary patterns for 0-F
3) Opcodes: switch on top 12 bits, decode nibbles, execute with flags
4) Timers: decrement every 16.67ms (60 Hz), separate delay/sound
5) Display: canvas 64x32, scale to fit, clear and draw frame
6) Sprite: load byte array, 8 bits per row, XOR to display, set VF if collision

11) File loader: FileReader API, parse hex bytes, load into memory
12) Step-by-step: single-step mode, pause state

I will create the single HTML file with all CSS and JS inline.
